title: Selector determinism + replay tests (kernel auto-selection v2)
author: Anika Gupta
release_notes: Internal: adds determinism/replay coverage for kernel auto-selection v2 selector; no runtime behavior change (tests + CI only).
body: Summary: Adds deterministic replay tests for the kernel auto-selection v2 selector to guarantee identical selection outcomes given identical inputs (model family tags, seq-length regime/buckets, GPU SKU normalization, and rollout gate state). This PR also wires the tests into CI so we catch nondeterminism regressions before canary/1.21 train. Context: Kernel auto-selection v2 is intentionally rule-based for explainability and rollback safety (see ADR-017). We’ve had a few sources of accidental nondeterminism during early integration (iteration order over hash maps when building candidate lists; implicit default ordering when multiple kernels tie; and floating-point feature scoring paths in debug builds). These issues are hard to spot with regular unit tests because they often only manifest across compiler/STL/arch combos. What’s in this PR: (1) Determinism contract tests: new `SelectorDeterminismTest` suite that runs the selector N times over the same request envelope and asserts a stable `SelectionDecision` (selected kernel id + ordered candidate list + fallback reason) across runs. Includes randomized-but-seeded permutations of candidate registry insertion order to ensure we don’t accidentally rely on map iteration order. (2) Replay fixtures: introduces a small corpus of “selection trace” fixtures (JSONL) produced from the selector debug dump mode; each fixture encodes inputs (model_id, model_family, arch tags, prefill_tokens, decode_tokens, seq_bucket, gpu_sku, cuda/driver tuple, gates/allowlist state) and expected outputs. The replay test loads fixtures and validates the decision is byte-for-byte identical, including the `reason_code` and `tie_breaker` fields. (3) Tie-breaking rule assertions: adds explicit checks for tie-breaking precedence (kernel priority > stable kernel id lexical > fallback precedence) and ensures candidate ordering is stable across platforms. (4) CI wiring: adds a new CI job `runtime-selector-determinism` that runs the determinism suite under clang and gcc configurations (Linux), with ASAN disabled (to keep runtime stable) and with `RW_SELECTOR_DETERMINISM_SEED=0x5EED` pinned. The job is required on `main` and on `release/*` branches. Notes: These tests do not change selector logic used in production; they only assert invariants and will fail if a future change introduces nondeterminism. Follow-ups: We may want to expand fixture coverage once GPU-SKU denylist rules land broadly (ENG-4823) and once scheduler-provided workload hints are integrated (PR-28502). Testing: `bazel test //runtime/kernel_selector:selector_determinism_test` and `bazel test //runtime/kernel_selector:selector_replay_test`. CI: new job required; see checks below. Risk: Low. Test-only + CI changes. Potential downside is increased CI time (~2m 10s on current runners). Review focus: Please sanity check the determinism contract (what fields must be stable) and the fixture schema before we add more traces. Also confirm we’re not asserting on fields that are intentionally allowed to vary (e.g., timing/telemetry metadata).
commits: tests(kernel_selector): add determinism test harness + seeded permutation runner
tests(kernel_selector): add replay fixtures + JSONL loader + schema validation
kernel_selector(test): formalize tie-breaker ordering in expected decision assertions
docs(testing): note determinism contract + how to regenerate fixtures
review_conversation: Noah Patel: Can we be explicit about what constitutes “identical”? I don’t want these tests to start failing because we add a new debug-only field. Anika Gupta: Good call. I scoped equality to: `selected_kernel_id`, ordered `candidate_kernel_ids`, `fallback_path`, `reason_code`, and `tie_breaker`. Telemetry-only fields (timestamps, sampling) are excluded. Added a comment + helper `DecisionDeterminismKey()` to make this obvious. Jordan Lee: Replay fixtures include gates/allowlist state — are we depending on policy engine serialization order? Anika Gupta: Fixtures store policy inputs as normalized primitives (gate booleans + allowlist rule id). We don’t round-trip serialized policy bundles, so we shouldn’t be sensitive to serialization ordering. Added schema validation to reject unknown keys. Sahana Iyer: CI runtime increased; can we keep it under 3 minutes? Also, do we need both gcc and clang? Anika Gupta: The prior nondeterminism we hit reproduced only under clang with libc++ locally, so I’d like both. I reduced iterations from 200 -> 80 (still catches ordering bugs) and limited fixture corpus in CI to the “core” set (full corpus runs in nightly). Omar El-Sayed: Please add an assertion that candidate ordering is stable even when two kernels are “equivalent” so we don’t thrash selection distribution. Anika Gupta: Added explicit tie-breaker precedence assertion and a regression case where two kernels have the same priority but different ids; candidate list ordering must be stable and chosen kernel must be the first. Approvals: Noah Patel (approved), Jordan Lee (approved), Sahana Iyer (approved with note to monitor CI time), Omar El-Sayed (approved).
merge_outcome: Merged via squash; commit: 8f4c2b1b2 (kernel_selector: determinism + replay tests).
